options.text: This solution installs workbook(s) to help you gain insights into the telemetry collected in Microsoft Sentinel. After installing the solution, start using the workbook in Manage solution view.
This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, create and enable analytic rules in Manage solution view.

elements.name: analytic1
elements.label: AuditD - A user account created and then deleted in a short period of time

options.text:
Identifies creation and removal of user accounts on the host within an hour by default.
 Consider changing the "timeDifmin" variable to adjust time difference between user creation and deletion.
 To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
    -w /usr/sbin/useradd -p x -k user_mgmt_useradd
    -w /usr/sbin/userdel -p x -k user_mgmt_userdel
    -w /usr/sbin/adduser -p x -k user_mgmt_adduser
    -w /usr/sbin/deluser -p x -k user_mgmt_deluser

elements.name: analytic2
elements.label: AuditD - Boot directory modified

options.text:
The purpose of this query is to detect malicious changes within the boot folder that could compromise system security upon startup
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /boot/ -p wa -k boot_mod

elements.name: analytic3
elements.label: AuditD - Files briefly appeared in forbidden directories before being removed

options.text:
This query aims to detect multiple addition and removal activities originating from a user-specified list of forbidden directories
Fill the "keys" variable in the Kusto query with the keys you used in your AuditD rules.
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied for each directory you want to monitor:
  -w <path-to-dir> -p x -k <key>

elements.name: analytic4
elements.label: AuditD - Ftp connection detected

options.text:
This query is designed to flag FTP usage that could indicate malicious data transfer, such as infiltration or exfiltration
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /usr/bin/ftp -p x -k susp_activity_ftp

elements.name: analytic5
elements.label: AuditD - grub directory modified

options.text:
This query detect malicious changes within the GRUB folder that could alter the system startup process
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /boot/grub -p wa -k grub_mod

elements.name: analytic6
elements.label: AuditD - Hostname changed via setdomain or sethostname command execution

options.text:
This query detects hostname modifications performed by executing the setdomain or sethostname commands
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S sethostname -S setdomainname -F auid!=-1 -k net_domain_host_name_b64

elements.name: analytic7
elements.label: AuditD - hosts file changed

options.text:
This query detects any modifications to the hosts file
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rule must be applied:
  -w /etc/hosts -p wa -k net_conf_hosts

elements.name: analytic8
elements.label: AuditD - Massive user deletion detected

options.text:
Identifies bulk user deletion: several user accounts removed from the host.
 Consider changing "DeletedUsersTh" to adjust the count of deleted users.
 To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
    -w /usr/sbin/userdel -p x -k user_mgmt_userdel
    -w /usr/sbin/deluser -p x -k user_mgmt_deluser

elements.name: analytic9
elements.label: AuditD - Multiple chmod or chown execution attempts on distinct files

options.text:
This query detects chmod and chown execution attempts on various files per host
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S chmod -S fchmod -S fchmodat -F auid!=-1 -F exit!=0 -k file_mod_chmod
  -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S chown -S fchown -S fchownat -F auid!=-1 -F exit!=0 -k file_mod_chown
  -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S rename -S renameat -S truncate -S setxattr -S lsetxattr -S removexattr -S lremovexattr -F auid!=-1 -F exit!=0 -k file_mod_unsuccess

elements.name: analytic10
elements.label: AuditD - Multiple cron jobs ddded in a short period of time

options.text:
The purpose of this query is to detect numerous cron jobs being added within a brief timeframe
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /etc/cron.d/ -p wa -k cron_crond
  -w /etc/cron.daily/ -p wa -k cron_daily
  -w /etc/cron.hourly/ -p wa -k cron_hourly
  -w /etc/cron.monthly/ -p wa -k cron_monthly
  -w /etc/cron.weekly/ -p wa -k cron_weekly
  -w /etc/crontab -p wa -k cron_crontab
  -w /var/spool/cron/ -p wa -k cron_spool

elements.name: analytic11
elements.label: AuditD - Multiple execution from forbidden directories

options.text:
This query aims to detect multiple executions originating from a user-specified list of forbidden directories
Fill the "keys" variable in the Kusto query with the keys you used in your AuditD rules.
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied for each directory you want to monitor:
  -w <path-to-dir> -p x -k <key>

elements.name: analytic12
elements.label: AuditD - Multiple failed chmod or chown execution attempts

options.text:
This query detects failed chmod and chown execution attempts per host
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S chmod -S fchmod -S fchmodat -F auid!=-1 -F exit!=0 -k file_mod_chmod
  -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S chown -S fchown -S fchownat -F auid!=-1 -F exit!=0 -k file_mod_chown
  -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S rename -S renameat -S truncate -S setxattr -S lsetxattr -S removexattr -S lremovexattr -F auid!=-1 -F exit!=0 -k file_mod_unsuccess

elements.name: analytic13
elements.label: AuditD - Multiple failed file and directory modifications

options.text:
This query detects various other unsuccessfull file and directory modifications, including remove, unlink, and similar operations
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S rename -S renameat -S truncate -S setxattr -S lsetxattr -S removexattr -S lremovexattr -F auid!=-1 -F exit!=0 -k file_mod_unsuccess

elements.name: analytic14
elements.label: AuditD - Multiple files added to a forbidden directories

options.text:
The purpose of this query is to detect multiple files being added to a user-specified forbidden directories list
Fill the "keys" variable in the Kusto query with the keys you used in your AuditD rules.
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied for each directory you want to monitor:
  -w <path-to-dir> -p x -k <key>

elements.name: analytic15
elements.label: AuditD - Multiple kernel modules loaded and unloaded

options.text:
This query tracks multiple kernel operation events for each host
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /usr/bin/kmod -p x -k kern_kmod

elements.name: analytic16
elements.label: AuditD - Multiple nmap executions

options.text:
This query identifies the execution of nmap
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /usr/bin/nmap -p x -k susp_activity_nmap

elements.name: analytic17
elements.label: AuditD - Multiple user login failures

options.text:
This query is designed to detect repeated failed login attempts by users
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /var/log/faillog -p wa -k session_faillog
  -w /var/log/btmp -p wa -k session_btmp

elements.name: analytic18
elements.label: AuditD - netcat, socat, or nc Executed After Firewall Rules Are Altered

options.text:
This query identifies the execution of netcat, socat, or nc following a firewall change
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /usr/bin/nc -p x -k susp_netcat_exec
  -w /usr/bin/netcat -p x -k susp_netcat_exec
  -w /usr/bin/socat -p x -k susp_socat_exec
  -w /usr/sbin/nft -p x -k nftables_exec
  -w /usr/bin/firewall-cmd -p x -k firewall-cmd_exec
  -w /usr/sbin/ufw -p x -k ufw_exec'
  For Debian/Ubuntu:
  -w /usr/sbin/xtables-legacy-multi -p x -k iptables_exec
  For CentOS/RHEL:
  -w /usr/sbin/xtables-nft-multi -p x -k iptables_exec

elements.name: analytic19
elements.label: AuditD - Network-related file modified

options.text:
This query identifies various network-related file modifications, excluding the hostname and hosts files
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /etc/network/interfaces -p wa -k net_conf_interfaces
  -w /etc/netplan/ -p wa -k net_conf_netplan
  -w /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/ -p wa -k net_conf_network-scripts
  -w /etc/resolv.conf -p wa -k net_conf_resolv
  -w /etc/NetworkManager/NetworkManager.conf -p wa -k net_conf_nm
  -w /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/ -p wa -k net_conf_nm_connections

elements.name: analytic20
elements.label: AuditD - Security-related kernel modules unloaded or removed

options.text:
This query tracks security-related kernel modules that could expose the host to potential attacks
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /usr/bin/kmod -p x -k kern_kmod

elements.name: analytic21
elements.label: AuditD - Successful login after multiple failed attempts

options.text:
This query identifies successful login that occur after multiple failed login attempts from users
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /var/run/utmp -p wa -k session_utmp
  -w /var/log/wtmp -p wa -k session_wtmp
  -w /var/log/btmp -p wa -k session_btmp
  -w /var/log/lastlog -p wa -k session_lastlog
  -w /var/log/faillog -p wa -k session_faillog

elements.name: analytic22
elements.label: AuditD - System firewall. Multiple changes in firewall configuration

options.text:
This query detects multiple kind of firewall configuration changes for iptables, nftables, ufw, and firewalld
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /usr/sbin/nft -p x -k nftables_exec
  -w /usr/bin/firewall-cmd -p x -k firewall-cmd_exec
  -w /usr/sbin/ufw -p x -k ufw_exec'
  For Debian/Ubuntu: 
  -w /usr/sbin/xtables-legacy-multi -p x -k iptables_exec
  For CentOS/RHEL:
  -w /usr/sbin/xtables-nft-multi -p x -k iptables_exec

elements.name: analytic23
elements.label: AuditD - System firewall rules flushed or reset

options.text:
This query detects when firewall rules are flushed or reset for iptables, nftables, ufw, and firewalld
To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
  -w /usr/sbin/nft -p x -k nftables_exec
  -w /usr/bin/firewall-cmd -p x -k firewall-cmd_exec
  -w /usr/sbin/ufw -p x -k ufw_exec'
  For Debian/Ubuntu: 
  -w /usr/sbin/xtables-legacy-multi -p x -k iptables_exec
  For CentOS/RHEL: 
  -w /usr/sbin/xtables-nft-multi -p x -k iptables_exec

elements.name: analytic24
elements.label: AuditD - User added to specific group(s)

options.text:
Identifies users being added to a specific group(s).
 Consider changing "forbidGrps" variable to include other groups you want to monitor.
 To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
    -w /usr/sbin/useradd -p x -k user_mgmt_useradd
    -w /usr/sbin/adduser -p x -k user_mgmt_adduser
    -w /usr/sbin/usermod -p x -k user_mgmt_usermod

elements.name: analytic25
elements.label: AuditD - User was added to the sudo/wheel group

options.text:
Identifies user accounts that granted membership in the sudo or wheel group(s).
 To enable this rule, the following AuditD rules must be applied:
    -w /usr/sbin/useradd -p x -k user_mgmt_useradd
    -w /usr/sbin/adduser -p x -k user_mgmt_adduser
    -w /usr/sbin/usermod -p x -k user_mgmt_usermod
